title: Quantization artifact escrow, retention policy, and access playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines the product playbook and acceptance criteria for how Redwood Console will manage quantization calibration runs and their artifacts (FP8/INT8 profiles, calibration traces, accuracy validation reports). The goal is a repeatable, auditable 'artifact escrow' with TTL-driven retention, clear custody and RBAC, and developer-facing recovery/restore flows. This work ties into orchestration (run lifecycle), storage cost controls, and compliance requirements for regulated customers.

Context and goals:
- Calibration runs produce multiple artifact types: raw traces (KV cache dumps), intermediate calibration telemetry, quant-profiles (FP8/INT8), calibration metadata (seed/params), automated accuracy validation reports, and signed promotion bundles (release candidates).
- Customers need: immutable auditability for promoted artifacts, short-term ephemeral storage for exploratory sweeps, scoped sharing for cross-team evaluation, and a path to archive/restore for long-tail compliance.
- Console must expose both UI and API controls for retention, exports, and access.

Decisions made so far:
1) Retention model (TTL + class):
   - Ephemeral runs (developer/ad-hoc): default TTL = 7 days.
   - Sweep runs (parameter sweeps): default TTL = 30 days.
   - Promoted artifacts (signed profiles): infinite TTL (archived) until manually revoked.
   - Compliance archive (customer-requested export): stored outside ephemeral buckets in encrypted long-term store (S3 Glacier or equivalent) with separate access controls.
   Rationale: balances developer velocity with predictable storage cost for high-volume calibration campaigns.

2) Artifact immutability and signing:
   - When a run is promoted (UI button or API /runs/:id/promote), system produces a signed bundle (SHA256 + KMS signature) and marks the artifact 'promoted'. Promoted artifacts are read-only and cannot be garbage-collected by TTL.
   - Unpromoted artifacts remain mutable by the owning team for a short window (48 hours) to allow quick fixes, then transition to immutable until TTL expiry.

3) Ownership and RBAC model:
   - Primary roles: owner (creator team), reviewer (read access + annotate), auditor (read-only across tenant), runner-admin (manage retention and exports).
   - Access checks implemented at two layers: Console UI (route-level enforcement) and object store (pre-signed URLs scoped by artifact ACL).
   - API surfaces: /runs, /runs/:id/artifacts, /artifacts/:id/permissions.

4) Accuracy validation workflow and gating:
   - Each calibration run optionally attaches an accuracy validation job (reference eval suite). Validation outcomes: PASS / WARNING / FAIL.
   - Promotion to 'promoted' requires PASS or explicit override with audit reason. Overrides are logged and flagged for periodic review.

Implementation notes (product + infra):
- UI: Run detail page adds 'Retention' widget, 'Promote' CTA, and 'Export/Archive' flows. Draft wireframes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CAL/Artifact+Escrow+Playbook
- API: POST /runs/:id/promote (req body: {target_environment, sign=true, export=false}) and GET /artifacts/:id/metadata. API contract PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-spec/pull/416
- Storage: ephemeral S3 bucket per-campaign with lifecycle rules; promoted artifacts copied to a tenant-locked archive prefix with KMS key rotation. Engineering design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Quant+Artifact+Storage
- Search/indexing: artifact metadata written to Run Index (Elasticsearch) including tags: model, sweep-id, profile-type, eval-score, signer, TTL-expiry.

Acceptance criteria (must be met for release):
- Console: ability to change TTL per run and per-project via UI and API.
- Console: 'Promote' action produces signed artifact, marks immutable, and prevents TTL deletion.
- Backend: garbage collection process respects promoted flag and tenant-level overrides.
- Audit logs: all promote/override/export/restore actions written to audit log and surfaced in Console activity feed.
- RBAC: permissions API enforces role matrix and pre-signed URLs expire consistent with UI visibility.
- Accuracy gating: promotion disabled by default when validation FAIL; override requires audit entry.

Progress updates and open work (as of 2026-03-12):
- 2026-02-21 (Maya): Drafted initial product playbook and proposed TTL defaults. Shared with Eng and Security.
- 2026-02-26 (Diego): Product/Eng sync — agreed on signed-bundle approach and copy-on-promote archive strategy. Action: Eng to prototype promote flow and KMS signing.
- 2026-03-03 (Priya - Security review): Requested proof of key rotation handling and separation of duties between signer and promoter. Security review ticket created: SEC-1981.
- 2026-03-07 (Diego): Eng spike completed (runner:feature/promote-signed-bundle). Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rex-runner/pull/1234 (includes test harness for signing and GC behavior).
- 2026-03-10 (UX - Jonas): Wireframes updated to show 'Export to Archive' confirmation modal and audit reason capture on overrides. Mock: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Q2_archive_wireframes
- 2026-03-12 (Diego): Implemented API endpoint GET /artifacts/:id/metadata and added artifact index fields. Integration tests pending.

Trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Keep all artifacts immutable immediately; simpler GC but worse DX for quick iterations. Rejected in favor of short mutable window.
- Option B: No signed bundle on promote; simpler but insufficient for regulated audits. Rejected.
- Option C: Per-tenant custom TTL defaults. Chosen, but will require tenant-level settings UI and extra validation work.

Security and compliance notes:
- All promoted artifacts must be signed with tenant-scoped KMS keys; keys are rotated and key IDs are recorded in metadata.
- Audit trail must include who promoted, when, and what validation result was present.
- For customers with export-to-onprem requirements, implement encrypted export packages with manifest and integrity checksum.

API/DB contract (high level):
- Artifact metadata record fields (stored as flat columns in Run Index): artifact_id, run_id, profile_type, signer_kid, signed_at, validation_status, ttl_expiry, promoted_by, promoted_at, archive_location, object_storage_key, tags. (NOTE: metadata modeled as flattened columns to keep search performant.)

Operational concerns and SLOs:
- GC job must not block runtime serving; schedule as low-priority background worker with rate limits.
- Monitor: artifact_count, average_artifact_age, GC_deletion_rate, promoted_artifact_count. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd-artifacts
- Rollout: limit UI rollout to 10% tenants, validate storage savings and audit logs for 2 weeks, then ramp.

Acceptance tests and QA plan:
- E2E tests that create calibration runs, attach validation, attempt promote on PASS/FAIL, override with reason, and validate audit entries.
- Load test: generate 1k sweep runs with typical artifact sizes to ensure GC scales.
- Security test: attempt access via pre-signed URL after role removal; verify denial.

Open questions / follow-ups:
1) What is the default policy for runs created via the API vs Console? (Proposal: API-created runs inherit project defaults.)
2) Should promoted artifacts be eligible for cross-tenant sharing under special agreements? (Needs legal review.)
3) Export format for long-term compliance archive — manifest schema and encryption envelope standards.

- Engineering design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Quant+Artifact+Storage
- API contract PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-spec/pull/416
- Runner implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rex-runner/pull/1234
- UX mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Q2_archive_wireframes

Next steps (owner: Diego):
- Complete integration tests for GET /artifacts/:id/metadata and /runs/:id/promote (ETA 2026-03-19).
- Wire up audit log streaming to Console activity feed (ETA 2026-03-26).
- Coordinate with Security (SEC-1981) to finalize KMS key policy and separation-of-duties checks.

Longer-term roadmap items (out of scope for this ticket):
- Per-tenant archive storage quotas and billing surface.
- UI for tenant admins to define default TTLs and retention tiers.
- Cross-tenant artifact sharing with access agreements and billing split.

If you review this ticket, please leave feedback on: the proposed TTL defaults, immutability window, and the override/audit UX. For engineering feedback include any performance concerns for the GC job or metadata indexing.
